findings.issue: The spaces in the spaced jp sentence were transcribed as きごう ('symbol') three times, inserting nonexistent syllables into the phonetic reading (wa-ta-shi-wa-KI-GO-U-ma-i-a-sa...).
findings.current: わたしわきごうまいあさきごうぱんをきごうたべる
findings.suggested: わたしわまいあさぱんをたべる

findings.issue: Same space-token artifact as kana: 'kigou' inserted three times into the romanization. This is beyond the known punctuation/katakana romaji issue — it adds phantom syllables.
Whitespace tokens (indices 2, 5, 8) carry the reading きごう ('symbol'). A space has no reading; this is the root cause of the corrupted kana/romaji and would break furigana/TTS.

The 'Quanto a...' device is the corpus mirror for は, but here the phrase is 交番に (locative に, no は). Rendering に as 'Quanto à' teaches a false particle mapping; elsewhere in the corpus に/で/まで phrases use prepositions (cf. 'No mar', 'Até a estação').
findings.current: Quanto à delegacia (lugar onde), policiais existem (em número de) dois.
findings.suggested: Na delegacia (lugar onde), policiais existem (em número de) dois.

findings.issue: Same defect as lit_pt: 'As for...' implies topic-は, but 交番に is a locative に phrase. The literal mirror misrepresents the particle's function.
findings.current: As for the police station (the place where), there are two policemen.
findings.suggested: At the police station (the place where), there are two policemen.

findings.issue: この is strictly proximal ('this'); glossing it as 'this / that' conflates it with その/あの. The pt gloss ('este / esta') is correct, so the two glosses also disagree.
